typology_authority: Peter T. Daniels & William Bright, The World's Writing Systems (Oxford University Press, 1996)
sequencing_note: Two entry priorities coexist in the archive without one superseding the other: (1) the owner's stated instinct in HS-T009 Turn 5-6 (Kanji radicals alongside Arabic, Cyrillic, and Latin as a 4-layer cognitive stack), and (2) the Notebook Practice Protocol's Greek-first progression by structural distance from Latin (HS-F001, 100 Poems roadmap). Both tracks are modeled explicitly.

kanji-first-stack.description: Four-layer rotational exposure pairing distinct cognitive regimes with low visual overlap.

greek-first-protocol.description: Gradual progression starting from Greek alphabetic familiarity before introducing Cyrillic, Semitic abjads, kana, and logographic characters.

typological-distance.description: Twelve-script sequence ordered by structural distance from Latin, with Kanji run as a slow parallel track.

scripts.name: Latin
scripts.inventory_summary: 26 basic bicameral letters plus language-specific diacritics and historical graphs
scripts.encoded_unit: phoneme (consonants and vowels as equal segments)
scripts.cognitive_regime: High-speed linear phonemic parsing; control and drafting layer for English writers
scripts.ductus_notes: Bicameral ascender/x-height/baseline/descender proportions; distinguish Classical Roman majuscule/minuscule from Insular/Old English graphs (þ, ð, æ).

exemplars.name: A
exemplars.form_note: Majuscule two-diagonal apex + crossbar; minuscule two-storey or single-storey bowl

exemplars.name: M
exemplars.form_note: Four-stroke majuscule; double-arch minuscule anchored to x-height

exemplars.name: S
exemplars.form_note: Balanced double curve; historical long s (ſ) in older print/hands

exemplars.name: Thorn
exemplars.form_note: Old/Middle English runic graph with both ascender and descender

exemplars.name: Ash
exemplars.form_note: Fused ligature in Old English and Classical Latin diphthongs

scripts.name: Greek
scripts.inventory_summary: 24 bicameral letters (with word-final sigma ς) plus polytonic breathings and accents
scripts.encoded_unit: phoneme (first full consonant-and-vowel alphabet, c. 8th c. BCE)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Linear phonemic decoding with false-friend remapping against Latin shapes (Η, Ρ, Χ, Ν)
scripts.ductus_notes: Start minuscule strokes smoothly from x-height or ascender; note descenders on β, γ, ζ, η, μ, ρ, φ, χ, ψ and strict positional split between medial σ and word-final ς.

exemplars.name: Alpha
exemplars.form_note: Minuscule α drawn as a continuous single loop crossing at right

exemplars.name: Beta
exemplars.form_note: Minuscule β begins from below baseline descender up through two right bowls

exemplars.name: Gamma
exemplars.form_note: Minuscule γ dips below baseline in a narrow loop

exemplars.name: Delta
exemplars.form_note: Triangle majuscule; minuscule δ coils from bowl into left-curving top hook

exemplars.name: Epsilon
exemplars.form_note: Short mid-front vowel; compact twin-curve minuscule within x-height

exemplars.name: Zeta
exemplars.form_note: Single sweeping curve from top bar down into right-turning descender tail

exemplars.name: Eta
exemplars.form_note: False friend to Latin H; minuscule η has short left stem and long right descender

exemplars.name: Theta
exemplars.form_note: Tall oval reaching ascender line bisected by horizontal bar

exemplars.name: Lambda
exemplars.form_note: Long right-leaning main diagonal from ascender to baseline, propped by left leg

exemplars.name: Mu
exemplars.form_note: Left stem drops to descender line before rising into u-curve

exemplars.name: Xi
exemplars.form_note: Three horizontal tiers (majuscule); coiled three-bend vertical stroke ending in descender hook

exemplars.name: Pi
exemplars.form_note: Horizontal lintel over two legs anchored in x-height

exemplars.name: Rho
exemplars.form_note: False friend to Latin P; minuscule ρ rises from descender into single bowl

exemplars.name: Sigma
exemplars.form_note: σ initial/medial within x-height; ς strictly word-final with descender hook

exemplars.name: Phi
exemplars.form_note: Central ring pierced by vertical shaft spanning ascender to descender

exemplars.name: Chi
exemplars.form_note: Diagonal cross sitting across baseline down to descender

exemplars.name: Psi
exemplars.form_note: Upward cup at x-height pierced by central vertical stem to descender

exemplars.name: Omega
exemplars.form_note: Open horseshoe majuscule; rounded double-bowl minuscule ω on baseline

scripts.name: Cyrillic (Russian inventory)
scripts.inventory_summary: 33 bicameral letters in modern Russian (including palatalization/hard signs ь, ъ)
scripts.encoded_unit: phoneme plus palatalization-marking vowel pairs and signs
scripts.cognitive_regime: Defamiliarized phonemic mirror; distinguishes block print forms from connected Russian cursive where т/и/ш/м/л share similar peaks
scripts.ductus_notes: Block print mostly mirrors upright majuscules at x-height (except а, б, е, р, у, ф); Russian cursive differs sharply from print (e.g., cursive т resembles m, cursive д resembles g) — keep print and cursive drills separate.

exemplars.name: Be
exemplars.form_note: Minuscule б rises above x-height with top right-going flag

exemplars.name: Ve
exemplars.form_note: False friend to Latin B; minuscule в is scaled-down majuscule at x-height

exemplars.name: Ge
exemplars.form_note: Right-angle gallows stroke matching Greek Γ

exemplars.name: De
exemplars.form_note: Trapezoid/arch body sitting on horizontal bar with two short baseline descender feet

exemplars.name: Zhe
exemplars.form_note: Central vertical spine flanked by symmetric meeting diagonals

exemplars.name: I
exemplars.form_note: Reversed Latin N; diagonal rises bottom-left to top-right

exemplars.name: El
exemplars.form_note: Curved left leg sweeping to baseline + straight vertical right leg

exemplars.name: Pe
exemplars.form_note: Square doorway matching Greek Π

exemplars.name: Er
exemplars.form_note: False friend to Latin P; minuscule has descender stem

exemplars.name: U
exemplars.form_note: False friend to Latin y; diagonal fork descending left

exemplars.name: Sha
exemplars.form_note: Three upright prongs on flat baseline bar

exemplars.name: Shcha
exemplars.form_note: Like Ш with right-side descender loop/tick

exemplars.name: Yery
exemplars.form_note: Soft-sign bowl on left paired with vertical stem on right

exemplars.name: Myagkiy znak
exemplars.form_note: No independent vowel sound; softens preceding consonant

exemplars.name: Ya
exemplars.form_note: Reversed R; iotated vowel

scripts.name: Hebrew (Square & Cursive note)
scripts.inventory_summary: 22 consonant letters plus 5 word-final (sofit) forms (ך ם ן ף ץ); optional niqqud vowel points
scripts.encoded_unit: consonantal segment (typically organized in trilateral roots C1-C2-C3)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Root-pattern inference from right to left; readers supply vowel melody from morphological template and context
scripts.ductus_notes: Square print (Ktav Ashuri) hangs from an upper ceiling line down to baseline; carefully distinguish near-minimal pairs ב/כ, ד/ר (corner overhang vs rounded shoulder), ה/ח/ת (left-leg gap and foot), and ו/ז/ן (width vs descender length). Modern handwritten cursive uses distinct rounded forms.

exemplars.name: Alef
exemplars.form_note: Primary diagonal top-left to bottom-right, plus upper-right arm and lower-left leg

exemplars.name: Bet / Vet
exemplars.form_note: Base extends slightly rightward past vertical spine (distinguishes from כ)

exemplars.name: Dalet
exemplars.form_note: Top bar overhangs rightward past vertical leg (distinguishes from rounded ר)

exemplars.name: He
exemplars.form_note: Top bar + right leg + detached short left leg (gap at top distinguishes from ח)

exemplars.name: Vav
exemplars.form_note: Short top hook + vertical stem to baseline (mater lectionis for o/u)

exemplars.name: Chet
exemplars.form_note: Closed arch/bridge connecting both vertical legs

exemplars.name: Yod
exemplars.form_note: Small suspended stroke hanging from ceiling line (never reaches baseline)

exemplars.name: Kaf / Khaf
exemplars.form_note: Rounded C-curve open to left; final ך drops straight below baseline

exemplars.name: Lamed
exemplars.form_note: Only Hebrew square letter with an ascender rising above the ceiling line

exemplars.name: Mem
exemplars.form_note: Open lower-left corner in medial מ; closed square in final ם

exemplars.name: Nun
exemplars.form_note: Narrow top + base in medial נ; long vertical descender in final ן

exemplars.name: Ayin
exemplars.form_note: Two upper arms converging toward baseline tail

exemplars.name: Pe / Fe
exemplars.form_note: Outer spiral tucking inward; final ף uncurls downward past baseline

exemplars.name: Tsadi
exemplars.form_note: Bent stem met by upper-right arm; final ץ drops straight below baseline

exemplars.name: Qof
exemplars.form_note: Rounded right arch + detached left vertical descender

exemplars.name: Resh
exemplars.form_note: Smooth rounded upper-right corner without overhang

exemplars.name: Shin / Sin
exemplars.form_note: Three upward branches from curved base; right dot = /ʃ/, left dot = /s/

exemplars.name: Tav
exemplars.form_note: Like ח/ה but left leg ends in an outward leftward foot

scripts.name: Arabic (Naskh study baseline)
scripts.inventory_summary: 28 consonant letters (3 long-vowel matres ا و ي), up to 4 contextual forms, mandatory لا ligature, optional harakat
scripts.encoded_unit: consonantal root and morphological pattern in mandatory cursive right-to-left joining
scripts.cognitive_regime: Connected word-shape (rasm) parsing + dot (i'jam) disambiguation + consonantal root reconstruction
scripts.ductus_notes: Write the continuous consonantal skeleton (rasm) right-to-left along the baseline before placing diacritical dots (i'jam) and vowel marks (harakat). Six non-connectors (ا د ذ ر ز و) join from the right but never link leftward to the next letter.

exemplars.name: Alif
exemplars.form_note: Tall vertical stroke; right-joining only (never connects leftward)

exemplars.name: Ba
exemplars.form_note: Shallow boat rasm on baseline with 1 dot below (compare ت 2 above, ث 3 above)

exemplars.name: Jim
exemplars.form_note: Wedge head above baseline + deep sub-baseline bowl in isolated/final; 1 dot inside/below (ح 0, خ 1 above)

exemplars.name: Dal
exemplars.form_note: Compact angled hook sitting on baseline; right-joining only (ذ adds 1 dot above)

exemplars.name: Ra
exemplars.form_note: Short tooth dipping smoothly below baseline; right-joining only (ز adds 1 dot above)

exemplars.name: Sin
exemplars.form_note: Three baseline teeth + deep final bowl (ش adds 3 dots above)

exemplars.name: Ayn
exemplars.form_note: Open right-facing c-cup in initial, closed loop in medial/final + deep sub-baseline curve

exemplars.name: Kaf
exemplars.form_note: Diagonal/S-beam in initial/medial (كـ); upright cradle with small inner kaf mark in isolated/final

exemplars.name: Lam
exemplars.form_note: Tall ascender descending into rounded bowl; forms mandatory ligature لا before Alif

exemplars.name: Mim
exemplars.form_note: Small closed loop on baseline with vertical or leftward tail in final/isolated

exemplars.name: Nun
exemplars.form_note: Single tooth + 1 dot above in initial/medial; deep sub-baseline cup in final/isolated

exemplars.name: Ha
exemplars.form_note: Four distinct contextual shapes: circle (isol.), double-loop (init.), figure-eight (med.), flag/loop (fin.)

exemplars.name: Waw
exemplars.form_note: Small head loop on baseline + sweeping sub-baseline tail; right-joining only

exemplars.name: Ya
exemplars.form_note: Duck-curved S-bowl below baseline in isolated/final; single tooth + 2 dots below in initial/medial

scripts.name: Hangul
scripts.inventory_summary: 14 basic consonant jamo + 10 basic vowel jamo composed into morphosyllabic square blocks (11,172 precomposed Unicode syllables)
scripts.encoded_unit: phonemic features arranged in two-dimensional CVC syllable blocks
scripts.cognitive_regime: Articulatory-feature transparency (consonant shapes model tongue/lip/throat posture; stroke addition marks aspiration) combined with square syllable pacing
scripts.ductus_notes: Stroke order strictly top-to-bottom and left-to-right inside an imaginary square (Tianzige): vertical vowels (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ) sit to the right of the initial consonant (가); horizontal vowels (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ) sit beneath it (고); final consonant (batchim) occupies the bottom tier (한).

exemplars.name: Giyeok / Kieuk
exemplars.form_note: Velar organ shape (tongue root blocking soft palate); extra horizontal stroke adds aspiration

exemplars.name: Nieun / Digeut / Tieut
exemplars.form_note: Coronal organ shape (tongue tip touching upper alveolar ridge) + progressive stroke addition

exemplars.name: Mieum / Bieup / Pieup
exemplars.form_note: Bilabial organ shape (closed mouth square)

exemplars.name: Siot / Jieut / Chieut
exemplars.form_note: Incisor/dental sibilant shape + top strokes

exemplars.name: Ieung / Hieut
exemplars.form_note: Throat outline: silent onset placeholder initially, /ŋ/ in final batchim

exemplars.glyph: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ
exemplars.name: Basic vowels
exemplars.form_note: Built on three philosophical strokes: vertical human (ㅣ), horizontal earth (ㅡ), short sun/heaven tick

scripts.name: Devanagari
scripts.inventory_summary: 11-14 independent vowels + 33-35 base consonants with inherent /a/ + dependent matras + virama (्) and conjunct ligatures
scripts.encoded_unit: akshara (orthographic syllable unit centered on consonant(s) + vowel)
scripts.cognitive_regime: phonetic-grid consonant matrix (velar, palatal, retroflex, dental, labial × voicing/aspiration) + non-linear vowel placement around the consonant core
scripts.ductus_notes: Draw the consonant body and vertical stem (danda) first, attach sub/super-linear vowel matras, and draw the horizontal head-line (shirorekha) LAST across the word (leaving prescribed breaks over ध, भ, थ, ष). Note visual vs logical order: short-i matra (ि) is written visually BEFORE its consonant.

exemplars.glyph: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ
exemplars.name: Independent vowels
exemplars.form_note: Used syllable-initially; post-consonantal vowels use dependent matras (ा ि ी ु ू)

exemplars.name: Velar varga
exemplars.form_note: Systematic five-column articulatory row: voiceless, aspirated, voiced, breathy-voiced, nasal

exemplars.name: Dental varga
exemplars.form_note: Contrast carefully with retroflex row ट ठ ड ढ ण

exemplars.name: Labial varga
exemplars.form_note: भ keeps an open loop at top-left interrupting the shirorekha

exemplars.name: Pad- (foot)
exemplars.form_note: Virama (्) cancels inherent /ə/ on final द्

scripts.name: Japanese Kana (Hiragana & Katakana)
scripts.inventory_summary: 46 basic hiragana + 46 basic katakana + dakuten/handakuten voicing marks and yoon palatalized digraphs
scripts.encoded_unit: mora (timed rhythmic beat: V, CV, palatalized CyV, geminate っ/ッ, moraic nasal ん/ン)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Isochronous mora timing; cursive hiragana carries grammar/inflection while angular katakana marks loanwords, emphasis, and sound effects
scripts.ductus_notes: Center every kana inside an equal square cell regardless of stroke count (1 to 4 strokes). Distinguish stroke endings: tome (clean stop), hane (flick toward next stroke), and harai (tapering sweep). Watch look-alike pairs: hiragana は/ほ, ぬ/め, る/ろ; katakana シ/ツ and ソ/ン (differentiated by stroke angle and start direction!).

exemplars.name: A
exemplars.form_note: Hiragana from cursive 安; katakana from left radical of 阿

exemplars.name: Ka
exemplars.form_note: Both derive from 加; dakuten が/ガ voices /k/ to /ɡ/

exemplars.name: Ki
exemplars.form_note: In handwriting, lower loop of き has a natural break (unlike connected gothic print fonts)

exemplars.glyph: し シ / つ ツ
exemplars.name: Shi / Tsu
exemplars.form_note: Katakana シ strokes move left-to-right upward; ツ strokes move top-to-bottom downward

exemplars.name: No
exemplars.form_note: Single sweeping stroke from 乃; ubiquitous Japanese genitive particle

exemplars.name: N
exemplars.form_note: Full moraic nasal occupying one rhythmic beat

scripts.name: Han Characters / Japanese Kanji
scripts.inventory_summary: 214 classical Kangxi radicals; 2,136 Japanese Joyo kanji; thousands of Classical Chinese literary graphs
scripts.cognitive_regime: Meaning-first spatial composition and visual-semantic compression; decouples conceptual graph from single spoken reading (Classical Chinese monosyllables vs Japanese on'yomi/kun'yomi)
scripts.ductus_notes: Balanced inside a Tianzige four-quadrant square so a 2-stroke character (人) and a 16-stroke character occupy identical area. Standard stroke order: top before bottom, left before right, horizontal before intersecting vertical, outside enclosure before inside before bottom closing stroke (日, 国).

exemplars.name: Person (ren / hito)
exemplars.form_note: Left-falling sweep + right-falling press; compresses to 亻 on left of compounds (休)

exemplars.name: Tree / Wood (mu / ki)
exemplars.form_note: Horizontal, vertical spine, left sweep, right press; doubles to 林 (grove), triples to 森 (forest)

exemplars.name: Root / Origin (ben / hon)
exemplars.form_note: Indicative stroke marking the base/root of 木

exemplars.name: Water (shui / mizu)
exemplars.form_note: Central hooked spine flanked by splashes; compresses to 3-drop radical 氵 on left

exemplars.name: Fire (huo / hi)
exemplars.form_note: Two side sparks + central flame; compresses to four base dots 灬 below

exemplars.name: Sun / Moon (ri, yue / hi, tsuki)
exemplars.form_note: Enclosures closed at bottom after inner horizontal bars; combine in 明 (bright)

exemplars.name: Mouth / Opening (kou / kuchi)
exemplars.form_note: Three strokes (left vertical, top+right corner, bottom close) — never drawn as a 1-stroke loop

exemplars.name: Heart-Mind (xin / kokoro)
exemplars.form_note: Curved base cradle + three dots; compresses to 忄 on left

exemplars.name: Speech / Word (yan / koto)
exemplars.form_note: Three upper bars +口 below; semantic radical across language/poetry/record graphs

exemplars.name: Foot / Suffice (zu / ashi, tariru)
exemplars.form_note: Upper box 口 + lower stepping strokes 止

exemplars.name: Way / Speak (dao / michi)
exemplars.form_note: Head 首 written first, walking radical 辶 written last underneath

scripts.name: Georgian (Mkhedruli)
scripts.inventory_summary: 33 unicameral letters with near-one-to-one phonemic correspondence
scripts.encoded_unit: phoneme (including three-way stop/affricate series: voiced, aspirated, ejective)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Unicameral rounded ductus; high phonemic transparency paired with unfamiliar curved silhouettes requiring fine ascender/descender discrimination
scripts.ductus_notes: No uppercase/lowercase distinction in ordinary prose; letter identity depends heavily on whether loops stay in x-height (ა, ო) or extend into ascenders (ბ, ზ, თ) or descenders (გ, დ, კ, ქ, წ).

exemplars.name: Ani
exemplars.form_note: Compact upward-curling hook inside x-height

exemplars.name: Bani
exemplars.form_note: Bottom bowl + ascender neck curving top-right

exemplars.name: Gani
exemplars.form_note: Upper small loop flowing into larger descender loop

exemplars.name: Mani
exemplars.form_note: Ascender stem curving down into closed baseline loop

scripts.name: Armenian
scripts.inventory_summary: 38 bicameral letters (36 devised by Mesrop Mashtots c. 405 CE + 2 medieval additions օ, ֆ)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Rhythmic vertical-stem cadence; several shapes echo Latin u/n/h/m arches with completely distinct phonological values
scripts.ductus_notes: Strong vertical picket rhythm; watch visual false friends with Latin (մ = /m/, ն = /n/, հ = /h/, ս = /s/, ա = /ɑ/).

exemplars.name: Ayb
exemplars.form_note: Three-stemmed trough resting on baseline

exemplars.name: Ben
exemplars.form_note: Tall ascender stem with crossbar

exemplars.name: Gim
exemplars.form_note: Top bowl with long descender stem

exemplars.name: Men
exemplars.form_note: U-trough rising into high right-hand hook

scripts.name: Ge'ez / Ethiopic (Fidel)
scripts.inventory_summary: ~26 base consonants × 7 vowel orders (approx. 182 core fidel syllabograms + labiovelars)
scripts.encoded_unit: consonant-vowel fused graph across 7 systematic vowel modifications
scripts.cognitive_regime: Tabular consonant × vowel grid cognition (source of Daniels' term 'abugida'); vowel rings, leg shortenings, and side ticks modify the base frame
scripts.ductus_notes: Upright monumental strokes between baseline and cap/x-height; drill horizontally across the 7 vowel orders (ä, u, i, a, e, ə/Ø, o) for each base consonant so modifications become systematic rather than 182 isolated signs.

exemplars.value: /lə, lu, li, la, le, lɨ~l, lo/

scripts.name: Cherokee Syllabary
scripts.encoded_unit: CV or V syllable (plus isolated /s/ sign Ꮝ)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Pure syllabic mapping using repurposed Latin/numeral-like silhouettes with zero phonetic overlap with English Latin values (high visual interference warning!)
scripts.ductus_notes: High interference with Latin shapes (Ꭰ = /a/, Ꭱ = /e/, Ꭲ = /i/, Ꮃ = /la/, Ᏼ = /yv/); must suppress automatic English letter-sound decoding.

exemplars.glyph: Ꭰ Ꭱ Ꭲ Ꭳ Ꭴ Ꭵ

exemplars.form_note: Anchor vowel row of the 85-sign syllabary

exemplars.form_note: Autonym sequence spelling Tsalagi (Cherokee)

scripts.name: Tifinagh (Neo-Tifinagh)
scripts.inventory_summary: 33 IRCAM Neo-Tifinagh geometric letters (evolved from ancient Libyco-Berber consonantal abjad)
scripts.encoded_unit: phoneme (modern IRCAM standard includes explicit vowel signs ⴰ ⵉ ⵓ ⴻ)
scripts.cognitive_regime: Geometric symmetry (circles, crosses, parallel bars, dots); tests spatial orientation and rotational invariance
scripts.ductus_notes: Unicameral geometric forms of uniform height; rotational/mirror pairs (ⵎ/ⵡ/ⵀ, ⴷ/ⴹ, ⵔ/ⵕ) require deliberate directional awareness.

exemplars.name: Vowels a, i, u, e
exemplars.form_note: Circle ⴰ, zigzag ⵉ, open cup ⵓ, neutral vowel ⴻ

exemplars.name: Yaz
exemplars.form_note: Emblematic Amazigh 'free person' glyph
